Five research questions

RQ1Yes, at one dayLightGBM 6.1% below HAR-RV; 5 of 7 pairs

How much of next-day realized volatility can be predicted, and do machine learning models improve on GARCH and HAR-RV?

LightGBM's QLIKE is 6.1% below HAR-RV's on average, significantly lower on 5 of 7 pairs. GARCH is 23% worse than HAR-RV. At 5 and 22 days LightGBM is 6% and 25% worse than HAR-RV.

  • QLIKE vs HAR-RV: Diebold–Mariano, 5%reports/tables/ml_volatility.csv
  • 5 and 22 days: Diebold–Mariano with overlapreports/tables/horizons_volatility.csv
RQ2Nobest AUC 0.507; calls beat chance on at most 1 of 7 pairs

Is the direction of next-day returns predictable beyond chance once look-ahead bias is removed?

The best average AUC is 0.507 (LightGBM · GMM experts), against 0.5 for a coin. No model's up/down calls beat chance on more than 1 of 7 pairs, and no return forecast beats a zero forecast (best out-of-sample R² -0.0005).

  • Up/down calls: Pesaran–Timmermann, 5%reports/tables/ml_direction.csv
  • Return forecasts: Diebold–Mariano vs zeroreports/tables/ml_returns.csv
RQ3Regimes yes, models noregimes help in 4 comparisons, hurt in 16

Do unsupervised methods recover economically meaningful regimes, and do regime-aware models do better?

A calm and a turbulent regime emerge: next-day volatility averages 8.7% a year in the calm one and 10.9% in the turbulent one. Adding regimes to a model helps significantly in 4 pair-model comparisons and hurts in 16.

  • Regime profiles: walk-forward labelsreports/tables/regimes_summary.csv
  • Regime-aware vs global: Diebold–Mariano, 5%reports/tables/ml_regime_vs_global.csv
RQ4No for tradingdirection signals' Sharpe -0.51 to -0.16; carry 0.24

Do forecast gains survive transaction costs, and give better risk-adjusted returns and more reliable risk estimates?

No direction signal makes money after costs: their Sharpe ratios run from -0.51 to -0.16. Carry earns 0.24 (p = 0.31). Better volatility forecasts do help risk: normal Value at Risk from LightGBM passes Kupiec's test on 64% of pair-sides, against 21% for EWMA.

  • Equal-risk portfolio: Newey–West t-testreports/tables/backtest_strategies.csv
  • 99% Value at Risk: Kupiec and Christoffersenreports/tables/risk_var.csv
RQ5Generative first, then discriminativeNaive Bayes ahead up to 252 days, logistic from 504

How does a generative classifier compare with a discriminative one as the training data grows?

On the high-volatility target Naive Bayes ranks days better with 252 training days or fewer; logistic regression catches up by 504 days and stays ahead. Naive Bayes is the worse calibrated of the two at every size.

  • Learning curves: pooled AUC and calibration errorreports/tables/ml_learning_curves.csv

Regimes

Weekly probability of the turbulent regime, each week from a model fitted only on earlier years. Shaded: the in-sample years before 2012 and the documented stress episodes.

Regime profiles, walk-forward labels

Backtest

An equal-risk portfolio of the seven pairs, net of half-spread costs, with carry earned on open positions. Pick a strategy to trace it; the others stay in grey.

Breakdown

How well each forecast holds a 10% volatility target

Value at Risk

99% one-day Value at Risk from each variance forecast, under a normal distribution or filtered historical simulation. A forecast passes when its exceedances match the 1% target (Kupiec) and do not cluster (Christoffersen).

Learning curves

A generative classifier (Gaussian Naive Bayes) against a discriminative one (logistic regression) as the training window grows, pooled over pairs. "full" is the expanding window used everywhere else.

Calibration

Slope of a logistic regression of the outcome on each direction model's log-odds, averaged over pairs, with a 95% interval. 1 means the probabilities are as confident as they should be; near 0 means their movements carry almost no information.

Features

Mean absolute SHAP value of LightGBM's inputs, averaged over pairs and yearly models.

Extra pairs

EUR/GBP, a cross with no dollar leg, and USD/INR, a managed currency, run through the same walk-forward tests as the core pairs but stay out of every core table and average. USD/INR has no free intraday data: its prices are the Federal Reserve's noon rates, so it has no volatility task, lacks the intraday features, and takes every input dated at the 17:00 close from the day before.

What the extra pairs show

  • EUR/GBP volatility: the best learning model (Ridge) is 1.3% below HAR-RV, not significantly (p = 0.53).
  • EUR/GBP direction: no model's up/down calls beat chance.
  • USD/INR direction: LightGBM (AUC 0.537) and Random forest (AUC 0.536) beat chance on up/down calls (Pesaran–Timmermann, 5%).
  • No strategy's profit is significant after costs (best Sharpe 0.31, p = 0.23).

USD/INR's price is one indicative quote taken after the onshore market has closed, so some of its predictability may be slow adjustment in a thin quote rather than a tradable edge.
